response.sql: SELECT AVG(t.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratio, AVG(t.line_item_count) AS avg_line_item_count FROM (SELECT oi.order_item_id, AVG(ili.product_price * 1.0 / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(ili.order_item_id) AS line_item_count FROM Order_Items oi LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items ili ON ili.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id GROUP BY oi.order_item_id) t;

assumptions.assumption: Invoice line items belong to an order item through order_item_id alone. Each line item counts once, whichever invoice it is on.
A ratio is missing when product_price or derived_total_cost is NULL. A derived_total_cost of 0 is also treated as missing (via NULLIF) so the division doesn't error.

The line-item count includes every line item, even those whose ratio is missing. Order items with no line items count as 0 in the average count. Their average ratio is NULL, so the outer AVG ignores them.
